explore.heading: Browse through any repository.
explore.description: Every account on the Atmosphere keeps its records in a public PDS. Browse collections, inspect identity history, follow backlinks, and edit your own records — all without leaving the browser.

extensionPage.heroTitle: Jump between Atmosphere clients in one click
extensionPage.heroBody: Land on a Bluesky post and want to read it in Deer? Click the leaf in your toolbar — the popup detects the AT URI on the page and offers every app that can render it. Pick a favorite once and let auto-redirect handle the rest.
extensionPage.oneClickTitle: Every app that renders the record, one click away
extensionPage.oneClickBody1: The popup picks up whatever AT URI is on the page and surfaces a recommended client at the top, plus every other waypoint that supports that lexicon — from Bluesky and Deer to Leaflet, Tangled, Margin, Grain, and the rest of the catalog.
extensionPage.oneClickBody2: Each row links straight to the equivalent page on the other client, so there's no copy-pasting, no fiddling with URL schemes, no re-resolving handles.
extensionPage.inspectTitle: See the AT URI under everything
extensionPage.inspectBody1: Switch to the Inspect tab to read the underlying record: the DID behind the handle, the PDS hosting it, the lexicon collection, and the count of inbound backlinks pointing at it.
extensionPage.inspectBody2: Click any field to copy it, or jump straight into the Atmosphere Explorer to read the raw JSON. The same data Bluesky's API serves, surfaced inline as you browse.
extensionPage.autoTitle: Set it once. Every link opens where you want.
extensionPage.autoBody1: Pick a preferred client for each kind of record — posts in Deer, documents in Leaflet, repositories in Tangled — and the extension transparently sends you there whenever you click an Atmosphere link from anywhere on the web.
extensionPage.autoBody2: Preferences are per-lexicon and per-device. Disable auto-redirect for one collection without losing the others, or turn the whole thing off and the extension goes back to a popup-only tool.
extensionPage.contextTitle: Even raw URIs on random pages become first-class links
extensionPage.contextBody1: The extension registers a context menu on any text that looks like an at:// URI. Right-click it and you can open it in your recommended app, inspect it on aturi.to, or copy a clean universal link pointing at the same record.
extensionPage.contextBody2: Useful in DMs, READMEs, JSON viewers, dev tools — anywhere an AT URI shows up in plain text instead of a styled link.
extensionPage.localFirstTitle: No account required. No telemetry. No background network calls.
extensionPage.localFirstBody: The extension only talks to your PDS when you actively trigger it — click the popup, hit Inspect, or follow a context-menu jump. Preferences stay in your browser's local storage; nothing is uploaded. <link>Read the privacy policy</link>.

terms.tos1Body: aturi.to is a free link routing service that allows users to share Atmosphere content and let recipients choose which client to view it in. We do not host, store, or modify any Atmosphere content.
terms.tos2Intro: You may use aturi.to to share links to Atmosphere content. You must not use the service to:
terms.tos2List3: Attempt to disrupt or compromise the service
terms.tos2List4: Impersonate others or misrepresent your affiliation
terms.tos3Body: We provide aturi.to on an “as is” basis. We make no guarantees about service availability, uptime, or functionality. We may modify, suspend, or discontinue the service at any time without notice.
terms.tos4Body: aturi.to is provided free of charge. We are not liable for any damages arising from your use of the service, including but not limited to lost data, service interruptions, or inaccurate routing.
terms.priv1Intro: aturi.to collects minimal data to understand how the service is being used:
terms.priv1Analytics: Analytics: We use Vercel Analytics to collect anonymous usage statistics including:
terms.priv1List4: Device information (browser type, operating system, device type)
terms.priv1AnalyticsNote: Vercel Analytics does not use cookies and cannot track individual visitors across different days or websites. All visitor data is anonymized through temporary daily identifiers that automatically reset.
terms.priv1Logs: Server Logs: Standard web server logs may temporarily include IP addresses, timestamps, and URLs accessed for operational purposes.
terms.priv1NoTracking: We do not collect personal information, use tracking pixels, or employ invasive tracking technologies.
terms.priv2Intro: Any data we collect is used solely to:
terms.priv2List2: Understand usage patterns to improve the service
terms.priv2List3: Prevent abuse and ensure service stability
terms.priv2NoSale: We do not sell, rent, or share your data with third parties for marketing purposes.
terms.priv3Body: When you click a waypoint link, you'll be redirected to a third-party Atmosphere client (Bluesky, Blacksky, etc.). Each of these services has their own privacy policies and terms of service.
terms.priv4Body: We retain server logs for a maximum of 30 days. Anonymous analytics data may be retained indefinitely.
terms.priv5Body: Since we collect minimal personal data, there is little data to request or delete. If you have concerns about your privacy, please contact us through our <repo>repository</repo>.
terms.priv6Body: We may update this privacy policy from time to time. Changes will be reflected on this page with an updated “Last updated” date.
terms.contact: Questions or concerns? Visit our <repo>repository</repo> or contact <site>atpota.to</site>.

universalLinks.heroBody: Drop an aturi.to link anywhere — a DM, a footer, a bio. Your visitors land on a friendly preview of the record and pick the Atmosphere client they want to open it in. No client lock-in. No sign-up. Every record, profile, list, and feed resolves to the right destination across 25+ curated clients.
universalLinks.anatomyBody1: Every aturi.to URL follows the same pattern: the host, a handle or DID, the lexicon collection, and the record key. The same shape works for every record type — there's nothing to memorize beyond what an AT URI already looks like.
universalLinks.anatomyBody2: Drop the collection and the rkey, and you get a profile link. Drop just the rkey, and you get a collection index. The path always degrades gracefully.
universalLinks.recordTypesTitle: Posts, profiles, lists, feeds, documents, repos, galleries…
universalLinks.recordTypesBody: If a lexicon has a public record, aturi.to has a URL for it. The same handle/collection/rkey pattern resolves whether the record lives in app.bsky.feed.post, pub.leaflet.document, sh.tangled.repo, or something brand new the ecosystem invented last week.
universalLinks.pickerTitle: A friendly landing page for every record
universalLinks.pickerBody1: Recipients land on a clean preview with a recommended client pinned at the top and every alternative listed below. They can read what the record is, decide where to open it, and never get stranded in an app they don't use.
universalLinks.pickerBody2: Each link is a real, indexable URL — embeds get OpenGraph cards, link unfurlers get a real title and description, and bookmarks survive client churn.
universalLinks.prefsTitle: Signed in? Your defaults travel with you.
universalLinks.prefsBody1: Sign in with your atproto handle and aturi.to remembers your preferred client for each record type. The next time you follow a universal link, the picker auto-resolves to your favorite app — no extra clicks, on any device you sign in to.
universalLinks.prefsBody2: Want to share a link that forces a specific client? Add a ?via= query param. Want to give your recipient the picker back? Drop it. The default-vs-override decision lives in the URL, not in the app.
universalLinks.prefsSyncedNote: Synced to your repo · works on every device you sign in to.
universalLinks.shareTitle: The link people can actually paste into anything
universalLinks.shareBody: An aturi.to URL is short, readable, and copy-pasteable. It works in Bluesky posts, group chats, blog footers, business cards, QR codes, podcast show notes — anywhere a regular link belongs.
